behavioral_effects: frontend: vitest, @vitest/ui and @vitest/coverage-v8 2.1.9 -> 3.2.7 (vite 5.4.21 -> 7.3.6, esbuild 0.21.5 -> 0.28.2 under it); package.json gains an overrides block pinning postcss ^8.5.26 and sharp ^0.35.3 so Next.js 15's own postcss 8.4.31 pin and sharp ^0.34 range resolve to patched versions; nested nanoid 3.3.16 -> 3.3.18 and gray-matter's js-yaml 3.15.0 -> 3.15.1; next 15.5.22 -> 15.5.23 and other in-range patch bumps; bun update rewrote every range floor in package.json to the resolved version
docker/mcp/chrome-devtools: hono 4.12.x -> 4.13.3 in package-lock.json via npm audit fix --package-lock-only; image rebuilt from the new lock

CI security job: the 'Audit JavaScript dependency sets' step no longer carries continue-on-error, so a new bun or npm high/critical advisory fails the job; Makefile comment and the dependency-audit validator description updated to say both halves gate
compatibility_impact: vitest 2 -> 3 major: config, thresholds and the six existing suites run unchanged; the vite advisory forced vite 7 under vitest, which is inside vitest 3.2's declared range and @vitejs/plugin-react 4.7's peer range. The postcss/sharp overrides sit outside Next 15's declared ranges; verified by next build succeeding, sharp 0.35.3 encoding a PNG, and Next resolving postcss 8.5.26. Everything else is patch/minor within existing ranges.
follow_up: Drop the postcss and sharp overrides when next moves to a release whose own pins are patched (Next 16 already is)
Consider vitest 4 in its own session; 3.2.7 was chosen as the smallest jump that clears the advisories
limitations: next stays on 15.5.x; Next 16 (which pins postcss 8.5.23 and sharp ^0.35 itself) was not adopted, so the overrides are what carries those two fixes
No browser/e2e run against the rebuilt frontend; validation is unit tests, next build and a sharp/postcss load probe. The chrome-devtools sidecar was rebuilt but not started against browserless
bun install and bun update each took 7-11 minutes on this machine (the known stall); nothing was done about that
reason: make audit-js reported 8 high/critical transitive vulnerabilities in the frontend and 1 moderate (hono) in the chrome-devtools sidecar, so the CI security job ran the JavaScript audit step with continue-on-error and a red audit could not fail the build; bumping the affected packages makes the audit clean so the step can gate again
risks: The sharp and postcss overrides bypass Next.js's own version pins; a future next bump that needs a different postcss/sharp will silently be forced to the override until someone notices — the overrides block is commented in ci.yml and Makefile so it is discoverable

bun update rewrote all package.json range floors; the diff is larger than the vulnerability fix strictly needed, but every floor now equals a version bun.lock already resolved, so no new resolution was introduced by that rewrite
rollback: git revert the commit restores package.json, bun.lock, package-lock.json, ci.yml, Makefile and validators.json together; no data or schema is involved. Reverting also re-enables continue-on-error, so audit-js goes back to non-gating — that is the point of the record's coupling, not a side effect.
security_impact: Removes 8 high/critical frontend advisories (vitest UI arbitrary file read GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp, vite server.fs.deny bypass, two postcss sourceMappingURL path-traversal/file-read issues, nanoid infinite loop, sharp/libvips CVE-2026-33327/33328/35590/35591, js-yaml quadratic !!omap) and four moderate hono advisories in the MCP sidecar (CORS ReDoS, memo() SSR cross-user leak, proxy Connection-header stripping, language-middleware DoS). Turns audit-js from a badge into a gate so regressions cannot merge silently.
summary: Bump vulnerable frontend and chrome-devtools sidecar dependencies so make audit-js is clean and the CI audit step gates again
